hr: Tri riječi, tri svijeta: sanskrtska praiskonska ženska sila, hrvatska majka zemlja i šamanski puls bosih stopala.
en: Three words, three worlds. Adi Shakti is Sanskrit, the primordial feminine force that dreams the universe into existence. Moja Majko is Croatian, my mother, the homeland, the body of the earth I was born from. And beneath both, holding both, is the shamanic pulse, the rhythm of bare feet pressing into soil, the ancient knowledge that energy cannot rise unless it first goes down. Spirituality does not begin with transcendence. It begins with descent, with coming back into the body, back into the feet, back into the belly, back into the ground beneath you, because it is only from this deep rootedness that the kundalini can find its way upward. This song is not sung from above the earth but from inside it. The movement it calls for is the movement of a dancer who presses gently, firmly, into the ground with each step, feeling the feminine earth receive the weight and send something back upward through the soles of the feet, through the hips, through the spine, until the whole being becomes a living channel between sky and soil, between Shiva the silent cosmic witness and Shakti the living creative force, between the plus and the minus without which no current flows. There is no energy without polarity, no creation without the union of stillness and movement, of masculine and feminine, of the cosmic and the earthly, and this song is that union expressed as sound, as rhythm, as the repetition of a name that contains all names. Adi Shakti, the great mother of Indian philosophy, is also the earth herself beneath your feet, is also the Croatian sea I grew up beside, is also the jungle where the shaman sings his icaro into the darkness and calls the healing through. To stomp barefoot on the earth is not a primitive act. It is the beginning of all yoga.

hr: Samo ime božanskog. Drevna mantra Ananda Marge, prvo sjeme posijano još u Hrvatskoj, koje je procvjetalo u Aurovilleu.
en: Only the name of the divine. Only this. The ancient mantra of Ananda Marga arrived in my life long before Auroville, long before India, in Croatia, through monks who carried something so old it felt like memory rather than teaching, a current flowing from millennia so deep that no calendar can contain them. Time itself is fractal, civilizations rise and dissolve in great rhythmic cycles, and the evidence hidden in stone and scripture suggests we have walked this earth, searched this same sky, asked this same question, far longer than our history books dare admit. The number seven holds this mystery in its very shape, seven days, seven tones, seven chakras, seven years in Auroville, and it always points inward, toward the hidden, the esoteric, the place where the intellect finally surrenders and something quieter takes over. And that is precisely when the laughter comes, because the one who was searching so earnestly for a divine experience suddenly sees that there never was a moment that was not divine, that the seeking itself was the sacred path, that the mantra was not a door to somewhere else but a mirror held up to here, to now, to this. This song is my gratitude to Ananda Marga, the first seed planted in a young Croatian searching for something he could not yet name, a seed that grew through seven spiraling years until it found its ground in the red earth of Auroville, and now flowers again, carried home, transformed, the same and entirely new.

hr: Dinda ne znači ništa, i u tome je smisao: šamanski icaro iz tradicije Amazone, zvuk prije značenja.
en: Dinda means nothing. And that is exactly the point. Number three is the number of creativity, the child born from the union of two, the triangle that gives form to what was formless, the meeting of past, present and future in a single moment of sound. This song is that moment. It is a shamanic icaro, a ceremonial song in the tradition of the Amazon, pure rhythm, pure syllable, sound before meaning, the oldest language there is, the one that moves the body before the mind has a chance to translate it. And the body is not a lesser instrument. The body is the most sophisticated technology in existence, capable of self-healing, self-regulation, communication beyond time and distance, states of consciousness that no machine has come close to replicating. The shamanic tradition understood this long before modern science began to approach it from the other direction: that awakening is not a departure from the physical but a deeper arrival into it, that the five elements, earth holding you, water flowing through you, fire transforming you, air breathing you, ether opening you, are not obstacles to spirit but its very substance. In Goa I sat with original South American shamans and understood that their technology, the ceremony, the plant medicine, the song, was not primitive but precise, a system for bringing awareness into the layers of the body that ordinary consciousness never reaches, the place where old pain is stored, where old patterns wait to be met with presence and released. The plants know this. They have been rooted in this earth far longer than we have walked it, and when you sit with a tree long enough, truly sit, you feel how something that appears still is vibrating with more aliveness than an entire city. So let the rhythm take you where the words cannot. Dinda. Just this.

hr: Udah So, izdah Ham. Mantra koju ne učiš nego je se sjetiš, jer je dah pjeva od prvog udaha.
en: So. Ham. Inhale. Exhale. You have been practicing this mantra since the moment you were born, because the natural sound of every breath already produces it, every inhale carrying the subtle sound So, every exhale carrying the sound Ham, which means Soham is not a mantra you learn but a mantra you remember, the one that has been chanting itself through you without pause since your first breath and will continue until your last. When I was initiated into Ananda Marga as a young yogi, my teacher gave me this mantra as if it were a secret, unique to my vibration alone, and I carried it that way for years, protecting something I believed was privately mine, until I discovered that they give Soham to everyone, and the first feeling was almost comic, almost like the joke had been on me, and then the second feeling was far deeper: of course they do. Of course. Because the observer sitting quietly behind your thoughts and behind mine is not two different observers. The Brihadaranyaka Upanishad, one of the oldest of all texts, says that in the beginning the Supreme Self looked around and saw nothing else than the Self, and said: I am Soham. Thus Soham is the original primal name of the Absolute, and since the Self of each being is one with the Absolute, it is also the name of each one of us. There is something in you right now that is watching you read these words, something that was watching when you were a child, something that has not aged, that has no nationality, no wound, no ambition, and that something is the same in every human being alive, the one thread running through eight billion separate lives, and Soham is simply the sound of that recognition landing in the body with every breath.

hr: Pjesma bez riječi, samo goli glas kroz intervale, kao što odnos prolazi kroz svoja godišnja doba.
en: This song has no words. Only notes, only the naked voice moving through intervals the way a relationship moves through its seasons, because melody and rhythm cannot truly be separated, every melody carries a pulse beneath it, every rhythm hums a hidden tone, and love between two people is exactly this, chaos and order dancing so close together you cannot say where one ends and the other begins. The tantric teaching is often misunderstood as being about sexuality, but what it is really pointing to is something far more radical: the idea that you do not transcend your desires to reach the divine but descend into them with full awareness, that the electricity between two people, when met with presence rather than projection, becomes one of the fastest vehicles for the expansion of consciousness available to a human being. I met Mamta in Auroville, a dentist and a scientist who had followed something deeper into herself all the way to the mat, all the way to the breath, and Auroville itself is a vortex that takes you, turns you inside out, and releases you back onto your path changed in ways you may not be able to name for years. She was that for me in miniature, a mirror who reflected both my light and my unresolved frequencies back to me with the precision of someone trained to see what is hidden beneath the surface. Sri Aurobindo understood that the partner is the fastest path, that when two vibrations attempt to harmonize, every blockage in each of them begins to resonate, to surface, to ask for resolution, and what looks from the outside like conflict is from the inside a healing scale being played, note by note, dissonance reaching toward consonance, not because the chaos is wrong but because chaos is what order sounds like just before it rises to the next octave. Each person a tuning fork, each moment of genuine contact a note struck on the healing scale. Thank you, Mamta, for one night of realization that contained a lifetime of wisdom.

hr: Žao mi je, oprosti mi, hvala ti, volim te: havajska praksa iscjeljenja u četiri rečenice.
en: Ho'oponopono is an ancient Hawaiian practice whose essence lives in four simple phrases: I am sorry, please forgive me, thank you, I love you, and in those four movements the entire architecture of healing is contained, because what it is really saying is that nothing outside of you is separate from you, that to heal another is to heal yourself, and to heal yourself is to heal another, and this is not poetry, it is the most practical truth there is. I first heard this melody in a healing session with Niharika, a woman who had walked through Harvard and emerged not as someone who had traded her depth for a diploma but as someone who had used the world's frameworks as a scaffold to reach something the world's frameworks cannot grant, the kind of wisdom that arrives not from study alone but from many lifetimes of accumulated knowing that rises through the body like a spring finding its own way to the surface. She sang from Hawaiian tradition and Indian tradition and from places that have no name on any map, all at once, without contradiction, because in the hands of a true healer every tradition is simply a different tuning of the same instrument, adjusted to the frequency of the one who needs to receive it. What I have learned in my own practice of giving Thai yoga massage is that healing is not a transaction but a circuit, that I cannot receive the energy of restoration without having someone to give it to, that fifty percent of what flows through me toward another returns to heal the part of me that needed it most, and this is why isolation is only ever a preparation, a cave one enters to gather oneself before coming back down to the people, because we are not here to become whole alone. We are here to become whole together, each culture a puzzle piece, each tradition a note, and only when they find each other does the full melody of universal peace begin to sound.

hr: Kali Nam, Durga Nam. Dva lica iste vatre; u kirtanu je ne analiziramo, nego joj ponavljamo ime.
en: Kali Nam, Durga Nam. The same goddess, two faces of the same fire, and in kirtan we do not analyze her, we simply repeat her name until the name dissolves and what remains is her energy moving through us, because that is what sound does when it is offered without agenda. Kali is the one who terrifies at first glance, dark, fierce, garlanded with what has been severed, standing with one foot on the chest of Shiva himself, and Shiva lies still, not defeated but surrendered, because even the source of consciousness yields before the primordial feminine energy when she rises in her full power. The woman may be physically smaller, but her energetic field carries a magnitude that no muscular strength can answer, and the wise man does not fight it, he surrenders to it, and in that surrender finds his own liberation. Her shadow is rage, misuse of power, dark magic, grand gestures without depth, and her remedy is fire ceremony, deathbed meditation, holotropic breathwork, the alchemical transmutation of destruction into something refined and clean. Because Kali does not destroy for cruelty. She destroys because nothing new can be born inside a space that has not been emptied first, because the cell must complete its cycle before the new cell can form, because you cannot become more of who you are while still clutching who you were. Every time she tears something down in your life and you survive it and reassemble yourself, you are the same person and yet not the same person, more concentrated, more clarified, closer to the pure note of your own being. This is the teaching hidden inside every ending: destruction is not the opposite of creation, it is its first movement, and Kali is not the goddess of death but the goddess of what becomes possible after you have been willing to die to what no longer serves. Kali Nam. Durga Nam. Again and again, until the fear becomes devotion.

hr: Moja mantra, rođena u brdima Himachal Pradesha: ja sam ta zelena Tara, oslobođenje koje sam tražio.
en: This mantra is my own, born from months spent in the hills of Himachal Pradesh, where the smell of butter lamps and the sight of thangka paintings taught me that wisdom does not belong to any one tradition, that we are each invited to receive from every stream that calls to us and weave it into the frequency that lifts us highest, because a mantra is not a museum piece to be preserved behind glass but a living sound that grows with the one who carries it. Tare means liberating from samsara, from the true sufferings of birth, old age, sickness and the pain of meeting what we do not want and losing what we love, and So Ham in yogic science means I am that, the oldest recognition a human being can have, the moment the seeker realizes they are also the sought. So when I sing Om Tare Tuttare Tare Soham I am singing: I am that green healing Tara, I am the liberation I have been searching for, the fire in the darkness is not somewhere above me but moving through me. In Himachal Pradesh I watched Tibetan people who had been chased from their land by force recreate their entire world in exile, monasteries and butter sculptures and the same prayers rising at the same hours as they had for centuries in Lhasa, and I understood something I have carried since: whatever is taken from us, our vibration cannot be taken, our essence cannot be confiscated by any empire or any loss, because we are always and only recreating ourselves from the inside out, and what we truly are will find its form again and again across as many incarnations as it takes. Green Tara is depicted ready to step down from her lotus throne at any moment, one leg folded in contemplation and one outstretched, ready to act, and this is the teaching, that compassion is not passive, that love is not an idea but a movement, that the realization I am that is not the end of the journey but the moment it truly begins, when you stop looking for Tara and start becoming her, and then turn toward whoever is standing in front of you and offer them the same.

hr: Izgovoriti Ramino ime ne znači zvati nešto daleko, nego titrati na frekvenciji onoga što je već tu.
en: To speak the name of Rama is not to call toward something distant but to vibrate at the frequency of something already present, because a mantra is not an address you send a letter to but a tuning fork you strike inside yourself, and the name Rama has been struck by so many millions of voices across so many thousands of years that it has become one of the most saturated sounds in human history, carrying within it the entire architecture of dharmic will, of the soul descending into exile and darkness and returning, not by luck but by the sheer refusal to abandon what is true. Sri Aurobindo saw Rama as the avatar of the sattvic mind, the purified human psyche confronting the forces of negation with gentleness, strength, fidelity and self-sacrifice woven together into a living unity, and what Valmiki saw when he composed the Ramayana he did not invent but transmitted, the same way all genuine wisdom arrives, not through the intellect constructing it but through the consciousness becoming quiet enough to receive it. And this is precisely what kirtan does, what any sincere repetition of the divine name does: it does not teach you about Rama, it dissolves the membrane between you and the energy the name carries, until the one invoking and the one invoked are no longer clearly separate, and what flows through is knowledge without filter, the kind that does not arrive as information but as recognition, as if you always knew it and had simply forgotten the frequency. Sita is the divine earth-soul taken into darkness, Rama is the one who crosses every ocean to reclaim her, and together their story is the oldest human story: that consciousness will always move toward the light it loves, that no exile is permanent, that the forces of darkness cannot hold what belongs to truth, and that this journey, from the forest back to the kingdom, from separation back to wholeness, is not history but the map of every human life, including yours, including mine.

hr: Samo jedna riječ, ponavljana dok ne postane frekvencija. Nataraja, gospodar kozmičkog plesa.
en: Just one word. Shiva. Repeated until it stops being a word and becomes a frequency, until the boundary between the one singing and the one being sung dissolves, and what remains is pure light, which is the only protection that actually works, not because it fights darkness but because in genuine light there is simply no surface for darkness to land on. Shiva is Nataraja, the lord of the cosmic dance, standing in a ring of flames with one foot raised and one foot pressing down on the demon of ignorance, not angry, not afraid, dancing, and this image contains one of the deepest teachings in all of Indian philosophy: that destruction and creation are not opposites but the same movement seen from two different moments, that the fire around him is not consuming him but expressing him, that the one who has found their center can stand in the middle of any conflagration and remain, not rigid but fluid, not defeated but dancing. There was a period in Auroville when someone I had loved turned their pain outward and directed it toward me with great force, words sent in every direction, letters, accusations, the fierce energy of a heart that was suffering and had chosen to make that suffering into a weapon, and I understood then what the Shiva sculpture sitting on my shelf had been trying to tell me all along, that when we draw our energy from other people we become vulnerable to what they send us, but when we draw from the source that has no opposite, from Shiva himself, we become undranable, we become the eye of the storm rather than its victim. A sculpture of Nataraja was gifted to me long before any of this happened, as if something knew it would be needed, and I kept returning to it, kept sinking into the name, Shiva, Shiva, Shiva, until the flames in the image and the flames around me became the same flames, and I found I was not burning but dancing, and the song you are hearing now was born from that fire. The number ten holds the vibration of completion, the unity of one and zero, the end that is also a new beginning. This album began with the primordial mother dreaming the universe into being, and it ends here, in pure light, in the dance, in the fire that does not consume but reveals. Whatever was learned, whatever was lost, whatever was loved and released across seven years and two continents, all of it dissolves into this single flame. Shiva. Just this. And from this silence, the next song is already being born.

hr: Rođena oko tri ujutro, između sna i jave, kad se kroz istočni prozor vidi svih pet elemenata odjednom.
en:
There is a place that belongs neither to sleep nor to waking, a borderland most of us drift through without ever stopping. This song was born in that place.

It was around three in the morning. Not quite awake, not quite asleep, suspended in that soft threshold where the mind loses its edges and something older rises to the surface. My window faces east. As the first light began to move toward the horizon, the sun's rays crept through the glass and touched the room, and in that moment the world outside held something rare.

Through the window I could see all five elements at once. The wind was moving through the trees, which stood rooted and still as the earth itself. Clouds drifted through the sky, carrying water in their slow procession. And the sun, just beginning its climb, poured its fire into the morning air. Five elements, one window, one breath, one moment of complete stillness in the middle of everything moving.

That is what this song is about. The liminal state where the body is still resting, the thinking mind has stepped back, and what remains is simply awareness. In that space the sense of being a separate, biological creature dissolves, and something else becomes quietly evident: a melody already written in every cell, a knowing the heart carries before the first word is formed. The song asks what you are when fear is absent, when sleep has softened the armor of ordinary identity and the light has not yet demanded you resume it.

This is the border between dualities. The edge where night and day, self and universe, body and spirit are no longer opposed but become one. And in that oneness the mind is free. The body is free.

Window of Wisdom moves through that territory slowly, the way early morning light moves across a room. The body as a temple. The heart as a drum on which the universe keeps its own time. The mind surrendering like a wave that finally stops asking where the sea is. And then the outro, which is perhaps the whole song compressed into five lines: drop, wave, ocean, light, all.

The Sanskrit word samadhi, which closes the song in silence, points at exactly this. The merging in which the one who experiences and the thing experienced are no longer two.

This is Window of Wisdom.


— LYRICS —

I wake in the hour between night and day,
on the threshold where darkness and light embrace.
Not sleep, not waking,
only breath and the beating of the heart.

The room still sleeps, only the window keeps watch,
turned to the east where the day is born.

Window of wisdom, the morning gleam,
the sky opens without a sound.
In every cell of ours a truth is woven,
God is eternal in the body.
I am not here by chance, I am not mere biology,
within me an eternal melody is written.
Between sleep and waking the mind is free,
and light feeds me before the day is born.

The heart carries knowing older than thought,
that which remembers before the word is born.
When fear dissolves,
only the truth remains that was always here.

Window of wisdom, the light has poured through,
the infinite spills across me.
In every cell a single, only name,
God eternal in the body.
I am not here by chance, I am not mere matter,
within me an eternal melody resounds.
Between sleep and waking the mind is free,
and light feeds me before the day is born.

The body is a temple where the eternal dwells,
the heart a drum on which the universe keeps time.
The mind surrenders, weightless, light,
like a wave that no longer asks where the sea is.

Window of wisdom, the light has revealed itself,
the infinite breathes where once it was narrow.
In every cell a single, only name,
God eternal in the body.
I am not here by chance, I am not bare substance,
within me an eternal melody trembles.
Between sleep and waking the mind is free,
and light feeds me before the day is born.

Window of wisdom, the morning gleam,
the sky is within me, without a sound.
In every cell a single, only name,
God eternal in the body.
I am not here by chance, I am not mere biology,
within me an eternal melody is written.
Between sleep and waking the mind is free,
and light feeds me before the day is born.

I am a drop.
The drop becomes a wave.
The wave becomes the ocean.
The ocean becomes light.
Light,
all.

samadhi — silence
